newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Duma says Russian govt not fulfilling budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Duma says Russian govt not fulfilling budget plan.

text.p: The budget committee of the Russian State Duma, lower house of parliament, said on Monday the house should give the government a fail grade on its handling of the 1997 budget.

The committee, on the eve of debate about cutting 1997 spending, recommended the Duma pass a motion calling the government's fulfilment of the spending plan unsatisfactory. The government had allowed "a complete breakdown in the collection of budget revenues and changes to the structures of budget outlays," the draft resolution said.
The government wants to cut 108 trillion roubles, about one fifth of planned spending, from the 1996 budget, citing low tax collection.
Top Communist Party economist and Duma representative Yuri Maslyukov told a news conference half of the proposed cuts could be covered by finding news sources of income.

The budget committee also voted against a new issue of cash which would double money supply, and which is favoured by communist deputies, by passing a resolution asking a Duma leader not to submit such a bill to the committee.
The bill would authorise the printing of 330 trillion roubles, in addition to Russia's current money supply (M2) which was 307.6 trillion as of March 1.
